backswingLimit.source: Spec §5.2 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-p2b2b2c1-single-ball-design.md), the user's account of the stance (2026-10-18) and the pre-flight gate (2026-10-18: θ_max at knee height, 64.9°); solved by scripts/fitStrokeShape.ts
backswingLimit.note: The shaft's greatest angle from vertical at the top of the backswing, at knee height: the angle at which the default mallet's head rises 0.48 m above its contact height ("about knee height", design §5.2), acos(cos θ_c − 0.48·s/ℓ) on the single-ball preset's canonical contact (θ_c = 0.0000°, s = 1, ℓ = 0.833575 m), 64.9021°. Bounds: 64° to 90°, the shaft horizontal.

effortTorque.note: The isometric torque τ_0. τ_0 and ω_max solved jointly (design §4.4): the weakest swing preset, single-ball, reaches the ceiling 9 m/s (1.1 × the CA's A4D 8.18 m/s, design §4.3) at intensity 1 from its body-limited top (θ_max = 64.9021°), and the drive's shaft there turns at κ·ω_max at contact, κ = 0.6667.

effortSpeed.note: The speed ω_max at which the player adds no more. τ_0 and ω_max solved jointly (design §4.4): the weakest swing preset, single-ball, reaches the ceiling 9 m/s (1.1 × the CA's A4D 8.18 m/s, design §4.3) at intensity 1 from its body-limited top (θ_max = 64.9021°), and the drive's shaft there turns at κ·ω_max at contact, κ = 0.6667.

effortShare.note: κ = ⅔, the share of ω_max the drive's shaft uses at contact at full effort from its body-limited top, so the torque left at contact is a third of τ_0. A labelled placeholder (design §4.4); the gate sees ½ and ¾ beside it. Read only by scripts/fitStrokeShape.ts.

handAcceleration.source: The P2b.2b.2c.1 pre-flight gate (2026-10-18: the hands' advance profiled, not pushed): the hands' ramp is a body property, set for calibration, never by the player
handAcceleration.note: The hands' peak acceleration along aim a: the advance's ramp lasts W = V/a at the head's planned speed V along aim. 300 m/s² keeps the 10 ms ramp the advance had at 3 m/s. No source: a calibration value awaiting data on players' hands.

ratio.note: The mean distance ratio of twelve pendulum drives, 4.23 ± 0.2 (the standard error of the mean), which the bounds take as the tolerance; Gugan's calculated ideal is 4.12 ± 0.04. The Croquet Association's drive band is 3.0–4.0 (Project Croquet Dynamics), recorded beside the target and not fitted to; the band's top, 4.0, sits just below this target's lower bound, 4.03, a gap recorded and not resolved (P2b.2b.2c.2 design §5.1).

speed.note: "The drives were of modest strength, with a mallet speed of about 3 m/s".

ratio.note: The mean distance ratio of twelve 'jab' stop-shots, 7.15 ± 0.6 (the standard error of the mean), which the bounds take as the tolerance; the scatter of single strokes is about ± 2.0. The Croquet Association's stop band is 4.1–6.2 (Project Croquet Dynamics, C3S, C10S and C20S), recorded beside the target and not fitted to.

speed.note: Gugan 5 states no mallet speed for the stop-shots, only that they "were of similar strength" to the drives, whose mallet speed is about 3 m/s; the stop is therefore fitted at 3 m/s.
